subject: [Urgent] HealthBridge 429 surge — quota routing loop suspected
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@healthbridge.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Cc: platform_ops@healthbridge.com
Date: 2027-04-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: 429 surge and retry storm — acute service impact

Hi Priya,

We started seeing a spike of 429 responses from Redwood around 09:00 PST this morning. Upstream retries have kicked in and our ingestion pipeline is now seeing cascading timeouts — downstream workers are overloaded. The errors began right after our SRE team finished what they called an "org capacity realignment" (they moved several projects between tiers).

Attached is a CSV with a 10-minute sample (throttle-logs-20270402.csv) and a screenshot of our dashboard (screenshot-429.png). Key points from our side:
- 429s started at ~08:58 PST and peaked between 09:05–09:20 (roughly 30–40% of requests).
- Error payloads reference "quota_exceeded" and sometimes "rate_limit_mismatch".
- Retries from our side increased RPS by ~3x and our queue latencies blew past SLA.

This is impacting our care notifications flow. Can you triage immediately? Please escalate if this needs executive attention — our execs are pinging us for ETA.

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
Head of Platform — HealthBridge
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@healthbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-02T09:21:00Z
Subject: Re: 429 surge and retry storm — acute service impact

Hi Sophie — thanks for the data, and sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating to engineering and our on-call support right away. Next steps from Redwood side (initial):
1) Karthik (cc'd) will look at the tenant/org routing & quota assignment logs to confirm whether the recent tier moves created an aliasing or routing loop.
2) We'll check for any policy changes applied to your org/project IDs in the last 24 hours and roll back if we find a problematic mapping.
3) If we identify a mis-assigned limit, we'll push a temporary override to restore throughput and remove your retries.

Marissa, I know this customer is a mid-stage expansion (HB-3471) — please prepare the customer comms + exec brief if we need to offer credits.

Sophie, I'll update you within 30 minutes with what we find.

— Priya
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-02T09:33:00Z
Subject: Re: 429 surge and retry storm — acute service impact

On 2027-04-02 09:21, Priya Natarajan wrote:
> Karthik (cc'd) will look at the tenant/org routing & quota assignment logs to confirm whether the recent tier moves created an aliasing or routing loop.

I'm pulling the routing audit now. Quick notes from first-pass:
- I see a recent admin event at 2027-04-02T08:55:12Z where HealthBridge org (org_id: org_9872) had its default project moved from tier "standard-1" -> "standard-3" and two project aliases were rebound.
- There is an unexpected mapping where project alias pbx-ops (project_id: proj_7023) still points at the old quota profile while the org default picked up a more restrictive per-project guard. In short: requests that should inherit the org tier were being evaluated against an older/stricter project cap.
- This kind of mismatch will surface as rapid 429s for certain endpoints and, because our SDKs treat 429 as retriable, customer retries can create a self-reinforcing load spike.

Immediate remedial actions I'm proposing:
A) Apply an emergency rollback of the alias binding for proj_7023 to enforce the org-level profile. This will take ~8–12 minutes to propagate.
B) Temporarily relax the project-level guard for proj_7023 to stop hard 429s while we finish a safer rollback.
C) Create a short-lived ingress-rule on your org so retries are de-duped for 1 minute (preventing the surge) — low risk.

I'll start A + B now and report back when propagation completes.

— Karthik
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@healthbridge.com>
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-02T09:55:00Z
Subject: Re: 429 surge and retry storm — acute service impact

Sophie — quick update while engineering works through the fix.
- We're applying a rollback on alias binding + a temporary override as Karthik outlined. Expected containment in ~10 minutes; full normalization in ~30.
- If the rollback restores traffic we'll follow up with a post-incident writeup and proposed safeguards (validation on tier reassignments + a preflight policy check).
- If service still has elevated errors beyond 30 minutes we will offer a service credit and set an executive call.

I've looped in Michael (VP, Revenue) so our leadership is aware. We'll keep this in priority.

Marissa
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@healthbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-02T17:04:00Z
Subject: RE: 429 surge and retry storm — incident resolved and next steps

Sophie — final update and apologies again for the disruption.

What happened:
- A recent org/project tier reassignment created an aliasing condition where project proj_7023 evaluated against a stale, stricter quota profile while the org default was different. This produced targeted 429s on high-throughput endpoints and triggered a retry storm from your SDKs.

What we did (timeline):
- 09:33 UTC: Detection and diagnosis (routing audit).
- 09:38 UTC: Temporary override applied to proj_7023 to stop hard 429s.
- 09:46 UTC: Alias binding rollback completed; propagation confirmed by routing audit.
- 10:05 UTC: Health checks show successful reduction in 429s and queue latencies returning to normal.

Actions & mitigations going forward:
1) We're adding a preflight check to the tiering UI to reject ambiguous alias changes and require explicit confirmation for org-level vs. project-level overrides (ETA: 2 weeks).
2) We'll introduce an automatic safety override when a rollback is performed to avoid repeat retries (ETA: 3 days, hotfix window).
3) We'll provide a short postmortem with logs and the CSV we saw, and propose a one-time credit for the incident (Marissa will coordinate).

Please let us know if you'd like an executive call — Marissa and I are available this week. We'll attach the full trace and remediation notes in a shared folder (link below).

Shared folder: https://drive.redwood/users/priya/healthbridge-logs
Attached: throttle-logs-20270402.csv, screenshot-429.png

Thanks for your patience — we're treating this as a priority improvement to prevent recurrence.

— Priya
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
